answer: A beacon-and-chain rule keeps fakes out: before bidding above ten units, an agent lights a plume, a signal for the job, and writes it into a spiral log where each entry chains to the one before. Within a day the client echoes the beacon to confirm the work started, while two peers audit the chain. A missing plume, a broken link, or a silent client burns a 15-unit bond; 100 fakes need 100 beacons and 300 chained entries, risking 1,500 units.
